title: Ops briefing: slimline calendar & annotated gitlog for July patch wave
content:
Purpose:
Short operational briefing for the Jul patch wave. Lightweight calendar + an annotated gitlog to help on-call and release stewards answer questions fast. This is intentionally slim — focus on what to watch, easy rollback checkpoints, and the small list of risky commits.

Overview / key outcomes: 
- Goal: land hotfixes for tokenizer regression (customer-facing) and a perf tweak for batching heuristics.
- Risk profile: low-medium (one infra tweak touches batching selector; monitor tail latency).
- Window: 2026-07-12 09:00 - 14:00 PDT (targeted 3-hour blue-green with 1h observation).

Calendar (hourly outline):
- 08:15 PDT: Preflight standup (ops + eng). Quick checks: infra green, staging smoke pass, feature flags ready.
- 08:30 PDT: Cut snapshot of prod infra state and roll-forward escrow. Archive logs (s3://redwood-release-escrow/2026-07-12/).
- 09:00 PDT: Start rolling patch batch A (tokenizer hotfix) to 10% of traffic. Canary gates at 5, 10 percent.
- 10:00 PDT: Evaluate telemetry (error budget, p50/p95 token lat, model-serving errors). Decision: proceed to 50% or rollback.
- 11:00 PDT: If A is stable, push batch B (batching heuristics) to canary lanes. If not, initiate rollback sequence for A and pause B.
- 12:00 PDT: Ramp to 100% for stable batches, begin 60-minute observation window.
- 13:00 PDT: Post-rollout quick retro: ticket summary, customer alert status, and known follow-ups.
- 14:00 PDT: Close window; handoff to nightly steward.

Quick preflight checklist (to tick before 09:00):
- [ ] Staging smoke: full text-gen smoke + kv cache warm path (run smoke script /scripts/release/smoke.sh)
- [ ] Secrets & KMS: confirm rotation state & key accessibility for private deployments
- [ ] Capacity: reserved GPU pool health, node counts match sizing doc (dedicated capacity pool: dpool-3)
- [ ] Observability: dashboards loaded (release / latency / errors) and alert thresholds set to temporary stricter values
- [ ] Canary flags set and verified in feature flags console (flags: tokenizer-hotfix-canary, batching-v2-canary)
- [ ] Pager contacts: 1st + 2nd on-call confirmed; escalation path documented in RLSE-342
- [ ] Rollback artifact ready: docker image tag, infra manifest pinned, and precomputed migration-undo steps

Annotated gitlog (selected commits we will ship) — short notes + why they matter:
- commit 9f2d7a1 — tokenizer/fix-unicode-token-split 
  - Author: Emily Chen. Fixes splitting bug causing occasional client-side token mismatch. Customer impact: misaligned token counts in a small subset of languages. Low-risk, unit-tested. Staging smoke validated.

- commit b3c4e9f — serving/batching: heuristics-fallback-tweak
  - Author: Samir Gupta. Changes fallback path when batch size dips below threshold; affects batching selector for short requests. Risk: may alter p95 tail due to different batching cadence. Include extended p95 monitoring during canary.

- commit ddf0a2b — ci: release-artefact-tagging-improve
  - Author: Aisha Patel. Cosmetic but important for rollback: ensures image tags are fully reproducible. No runtime change.

- commit 8a7c123 — infra/k8s: readiness-probe-adjustment
  - Author: Ops team. Tweaks probe timeouts which change pod cycling behavior. Medium risk; validated in staging but watch pod churn during ramp.

Release notes (draft text to copy into customer-facing channel):
- Release: July 2026 patch wave (tokenizer & batching improvements)
- Highlights:
  * Fixed a tokenizer edge case that caused token miscounts for certain Unicode inputs — improves accuracy in multilingual payloads.
  * Tuned batching heuristics to improve throughput for lots of short requests, reducing average per-call cost in affected workloads.
- Known issues: small change to readiness probes may increase transient pod restarts during rollout; we will monitor and roll back if sustained errors are seen.
- Impact: no planned downtime; changes rolled out via canary. Customers using private on-prem packages should verify KMS keys remain accessible after rollout.

Rollback plan (fast-rollback, 10–15 minutes target):
- Immediate trigger conditions: >5% increase in 5xx errors vs baseline OR p95 latency increase >30% sustained for 5m OR customer-critical ticket flagged by CS.
- Steps:
  1) Flip canary flags off for the batch being rolled (tokenizer-hotfix-canary / batching-v2-canary).
  2) Trigger rollout to pinned previous image tag: redwood/repo:2026-07-05-stable (k8s manifest rollback).
  3) If rollback does not restore behavior in 10m, scale down new deployment and scale up old manually (k8s emergency script /scripts/release/rollback_emergency.sh).
  4) Notify stakeholders (pager, #rlse-ops, CS lead) and open incident bridge if customer impact observed.

Monitoring & signals (what to watch):
- Latency: p50, p95, p99 for text-generation endpoints (prefix: /v1/generate).
- Errors: 5xx rate, model-serving-internal-errors, tokenizer-exception counts.
- Infra: pod restart rate, OOMs, node CPU/GPU saturation (>85% sustained).
- Business signals: CS ticket volume tagged tokenizer, and any high-severity customer alerts.

Open questions / followups (notes-to-self):
- Is there an A/B test tag left on any client SDK that might still hit old code paths? (TODO: ./tools/scan-client-flags.sh)
- Confirm retention of debug logs for the 2h post-rollout window — do we need to extend to 4h for root-cause?
- Post-release: schedule a quick perf run against the replay corpus (replay/replay-2026-07) to measure cost delta.

Communications (templates):
- Customer push (short): "We rolled out July 2026 patches: tokenizer accuracy fix and batching improvement. No downtime expected; please reach out if you see tokenization mismatches or latency regressions."
- Internal incident blurb (if rollback): short timeline, culprit commits, immediate mitigation.

Appendix: quick commands
- Staging smoke: ./scripts/release/smoke.sh --staging
- Rollback (emergency): ./scripts/release/rollback_emergency.sh --tag=2026-07-05-stable
- Canary flag verification: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://flags.console/api/flags?name=tokenizer-hotfix-canary

Last notes: prioritize clear, short handovers. If you are the 2nd on-call and forced to step in mid-roll, the annotated gitlog above is the fastest way to get context. Keep alerts tight for the 60-minute observation window after 100% ramp.

-- Marcus R.
